 Judgment
Though these appeals are listed for admission, they are taken up for final disposal, with the consent of learned counsel for both the parties.

2. Both the claimants as well as NWKRTC are in appeal challenging judgment and award dated 31.12.2018 passed in MVC No.2742/2017 on the file of learned XI Addl. District Jude and Member,
Addl. MACT, Belagavi (for short, 'Tribunal').
3.

The claimants are in appeal in MFA No.100492/2020 praying for enhancement of compensation,
whereas NWKRTC is in appeal in MFA No.101437/2019 challenging the liability as well as quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

4. The claimants, who are the wife, children and father of deceased Sugriv B Karande, filed a claim petition NC: 2023:KHC-D:7519-DB under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the accidental death of deceased Sugriv B Karande, that took place on 08.09.2017 involving Force Trax Cruiser bearing registration No.MH-45/N-4327 and NWKRTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-25/F-3138.
It is stated that the deceased was aged 51 years and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month by doing masonry work.
It is further stated that deceased had undergone course in Masonry conducted by Maharashtra State Technical High School cum Industrial School, Solhapur.

sentences.text: The claimants were depending on the earning of the deceased.
5. On issuance of notice, respondent No.2 remained absent and placed exparte.
Respondent No.1-NWKRTC appeared through its counsel and filed statement of objections denying the entire claim petition averments.
It denied the allegation that the accident had occurred due to negligence of driver of NWKRTC.
It further contended that the accident occurred due to sole negligence of driver of Force Trax.
Thus, sought for dismissal of the claim petition.

Before the Tribunal, claimant No.1-wife of the deceased examined as PW1 apart from marking the documents as Exs.P1 to P10.

On behalf of the respondents, driver of NWKRTC examined as RW1,
but no documents were marked.

The Tribunal based on the material on record awarded a total compensation of Rs.17,78,500/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization on the following heads:
 Loss of dependency Rs.16,33,500/-
 Loss of consortium Rs. 40,000/-
 Loss of estate Rs. 15,000/-
 Funeral expenses Rs. 15,000/-

Loss of love and affection Rs. 75,000/-

7. While awarding the above compensation, the Tribunal assessed monthly income of the deceased at Rs.15,000/-, added 10% of the assessed income towards future prospects, applied multiplier of 11 as the deceased was aged 51 years and deducted 1/4th towards personal expenses of the deceased.
The Tribunal fixed contributory negligence on the part of NWRKTC at 80% and on driver of Force trax at 20%.

The appellant-Corporation is in appeal NC: 2023:KHC-D:7519-DB before this Court aggrieved by saddling of liability as well as quantum of compensation and the claimants are also in appeal praying for enhancement of compensation, not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

8. Heard the learned counsel Sri. Vitthal S Teli for the appellants/claimants and Sri. S.C. Bhuti,
learned counsel for the appellant/NWKRTC and perused the appeal papers along with original records.
9.

Learned counsel for the appellants/claimants would submit that the deceased was aged 51 years and had undergone masonry training course conducted by Maharashtra State Technical High School cum Industrial School, Solhapur as per Ex.P8.

sentences.text: He further submits that the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month by doing masonry work, but the Tribunal committed an error in assessing monthly income of the deceased at Rs.15,000/-, which is on the lower side.
Learned counsel further submits that the Tribunal saddled liability to an extent of 80% on NWKRTC and 20% on driver of Force Trax.
He further NC: 2023:KHC-D:7519-DB submits that the Tribunal rightly observed that it is for the claimants to recover compensation from either of the parties.

He also submits that the Tribunal committed an error in not awarding compensation on the head of parental and filial consortium as held by the Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Nanu Ram &
Others1.

10. Per contra, Sri. S.C. Learned counsel would submit that though the claimants produced Ex.P8- Certifiicate for having undergone training in masonry by the deceased, but no material is placed on record to show that the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.

In the absence of any material on record to establish the income of the deceased, the Tribunal is not justified in 2018 ACJ 2782 NC: 2023:KHC-D:7519-DB assessing income of the deceased at Rs.15,000/- per month, which is more than notional income fixed by KSLSA for the accident of the year 2017.
Thus, prays for re-assessing monthly income of the deceased by taking notional income fixed by KSLSA.

Bhuti would further submit that in respect of very same accident, High Court of Karnataka, Kalaburagi Bench, in the appeals filed by the claimants as well as NWKRTC, has fixed contributory negligence to an extent of 75% on NWKRTC and 25% on driver of Force Trax Cruiser.

Having heard the learned counsel for both the parties and on perusal of the appeal papers along with original records, the only point that would fall for consideration in these appeals, whether impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal requires interference at the hands of this Court in the facts and circumstances of the case?

Our answer to the above point would be in the affirmative for the following reasons:
14.

The occurrence of the accident on 08.09.2017 involving Force Trax Cruiser bearing registration No.MH- 45/N-4327 and NWKRTC Bus bearing registration No.KA- 25/F-3138 and resultant death of deceased Sugriv B Karande is not in dispute in these appeals.

15. The Tribunal on assessing the entire material on record held that both drivers of NWKRTC and Force Trax Cruiser are responsible for occurrence of the accident in question and saddled contributory negligence to an extent of 80% on NWKRTC and 20% on driver of Trax Cruiser.
The said finding requires modification in terms of the judgment dated 21.03.2022 in MFA No.200294/2020 & connected appeals passed by High Court of Karnataka, Kalaburagi Bench.

sentences.text: The said appeals were filed challenging the judgment and award passed by learned III Addl. Senior Civil Judge and Member, MACT-XII, Vijayapura in respect of very same accident.

Therefore, in terms of above said judgment and on the ground of partity, contributory negligence is modified to - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7519-DB an extent of 75% and 25% in respect of NWKRTC and driver of Force Trax Cruiser respectively.
16. As regards the quantum of compensation, the Tribunal committed an error in assessing monthly income of the deceased at Rs.15,000/-.

Admittedly, there is no material on record to establish the Kalpana W/O. Sugriv Karande vs The Divisional Controller on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42996630/

Therefore, it would be appropriate for this Court to assess notional income of the deceased at Rs.10,250/- per month.
17 . There is no dispute with regard to the age of the deceased as 51 years, multiplier of 11 and also deduction of 1/4th towards personal expenses of the deceased.

The - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7519-DB Tribunal has rightly added 10% of the assessed income towards future prospects, since the deceased was aged 51 years and self-employer and in terms of decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Others2.

Accordingly, the claimants would be entitled for compensation on the head of loss of dependency at Rs.11,16,225/- (Rs.10,250 + 10/100 x 12 x 11 x 3/4).
18.
Further, claimants would be entitled to Rs.40,000/- each towards spousal, parental and filial consortium as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Company Limited (supra).

Further, the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.15,000/-
towards funeral expenses and transportation of dead body, which is just and proper and same is not disturbed.

Thus, the claimants would be entitled for modified compensation on the following heads:

ORDER a) Both appeals are allowed in part.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to an extent that the claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.13,06,225/- as against Rs.17,78,500/- awarded by the Tribunal.
